blocks.text: How Italian Women Claimed Their Place in Modern Society

Gallerie d’Italia in Milan presents “LIBERE! 1946–2026. Le conquiste delle donne” ( FREE! 1946–2026. Women’s Hard-Won Rights) , an exhibition curated by Renata Ferri that traces almost eighty years of women’s achievements in Italy, beginning with the vote of June 2, 1946.
By Gaia Squarci. Cover Photo by Publifoto Archive, Intesa Sanpaolo

Through photographs from Italy’s major historical archives, the exhibition traces the social and cultural changes that led women toward emancipation. Running through the whole show is a tension between work and leisure, independence and tradition, captured in scenes of factory workers after World War II, office clerks of the economic boom, housewives, women casting their first votes, and girls screaming at a Beatles concert.
Then the focus shifts to the feminist movement and the battles over divorce and abortion, along with a tribute to women who left their mark on Italian culture, science, politics and the arts.

The final section brings together photographs and multimedia works by contemporary women artists. Above all, the show makes clear that rights are never handed out. They were won by earlier generations who fought for them, and they can be lost again at any time.
The exhibition “LIBERE! 1946–2026. Le conquiste delle donne” is on view at Gallerie d’Italia in Milan, Italy, until February 7, 2027.
